You have to subscribe to the subverse to begin with. If this becomes the status quo, then that is, by default, opting in. But more so as a packaged deal. Subscribing to the subverse subscribes you to mod messages.

Since you control what you are subscribed to, it's opt-in and opt-out isn't an option, if viewed that way.
Yeah but someone may only want mod messages to come from one subverse and not all of them.

So, we go back to the option of being able to disable them in your settings.

Basically, I think it would be fine if the setting was automatically on when you subscribed to the subverse, but you could turn it off in your settings anyway.

Or, even better, have a default general setting on your profile page that you set as the default for any subs you join. Then, if you decide a certain sub should be the opposite of your default choice (in your case, getting mod messages in one sub but not for the rest of them), you can do that.

Still, that defeats the purpose of what a mod message would be used for. It'd be like subscribing to a subverse and then having to opt-in to seeing content from that subverse. They are basically the same thing in this case. It has the potential to be abused, but with the open-ness of Voat (mod logs, among other things), such abuse would be open too and hopefully fixed promptly.

With the current system, I'd be fine with it being on by default as soon as you join a subverse.

How about with a limit of 1 message per month? This means if you subscribe to say 50 subverses, you can get maximum 50 messages per month from them all (which will happen over the course of a month, so not all at the same time). In addition, if you still feel it is spam, you can opt-out.
